claims.statement: Tom Allen issued a challenge offering to fight Jim Mace, Joe Coburn or any man in the world for $1,000 to $5,000.
claims.excerpt: a challenge, offering to fight Jim Mace, Joe Coburn, or any man in the world, for $1,000

claims.statement: Allen said he would fight Mace under London prize ring rules for $1,000 to $5,000 a side, in Kansas, New Orleans or Canada.
claims.excerpt: for from $1,000 to $5,000 a side, the fight to take place in Kansas, New Orleans

claims.statement: Allen offered to meet Mace's backers at Pittsburg or Cincinnati to sign articles, with a $500 deposit.
claims.excerpt: be ready to meet Mace or his backers from New York, at Pittsburg or

claims.statement: If Mace refused, Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn, wagering $2,500 to Coburn's $1,500, or to fight Ben Hogan for $1,000 to $5,000.
claims.excerpt: and will wager $2,500 to Coburn’s $1,500: or L will fight Ben Hogan

claims.statement: Mace sent word back that if Allen would fight, he would return to America and fight him on Allen's terms.
claims.excerpt: would return to America and tight Allen according w the latter

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Jem Mace in New Orleans in May 1870.
claims.excerpt: New Orleans, in May, 1870. In that contest ANen was defeated

claims.statement: Allen's last contest, against Mike McCoole, was on Chouteau Island, Illinois, in the fall of 1873.
